facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: TripAdvisor, Inc. enters the fourth quarter of 2026 with a lower-earning but lower-debt capital structure than a year ago. On the continuing-operations perimeter, LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 207.3 against 294.7 for FY2025, driven by Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026, while Experiences revenue fell 3% in the same quarter after growing earlier in the year. Debt principal has fallen from 1,185 at December 31, 2025 to 833.9 at September 30, 2026 because the 345.0 convertible notes were repaid in cash on April 1, 2026, so gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 only because EBITDA and debt fell together. Net of 706.8 of cash the ratio is 0.61x, but 396.8 of deferred merchant payables, amounts owed to experience operators after travel, sit against that cash, and on a cash-less-float basis net leverage is 2.53x. Free cash flow is negative on an LTM basis, interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x LTM, and the term loan has no financial covenant while the revolver carries a leverage maximum whose reported level is not printed in the 2026 filings. The TheFork sale added about 741.0 of net cash on November 1, 2026, after the balance sheet date, so the reported figures understate the post-sale cash position. Every ratio below rests on management Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, so the ratios are better read as a ceiling on earnings capacity than as a covenant calculation.

facts.label: Segment and earnings quality drivers
facts.text: Hotels and Other revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and 21% over nine months, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 41% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 (Q3 PR page:1 and page:14). Management attributes the decline to "the sustained acceleration of traffic acquisition headwinds negatively impacting this business due to the changes in the search landscape" (Q3 10-Q page:22), which reads as a structural rather than cyclical explanation (analyst reading). Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026 after growing 1% over nine months, with Adjusted EBITDA down 27% in Q3 2026; the 10-Q cites macro events, cancellations and search headwinds on the Tripadvisor point of sale (Q3 10-Q page:43 and page:49). Mechanism: the segment that supplies about 69% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is the one in structural decline, and the growth segment's LTM margin is 6.8% against 23.0% for Hotels and Other, so group margin falls as mix shifts even before any further decline in Hotels and Other. Credit implication: debt capacity depends on how fast Hotels and Other earnings erode against how fast Experiences margin can expand; the November 4, 2026 restructuring plan (costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million, Q3 10-Q page:37) targets the cost base but management's claimed savings are a release-only statement (Q3 PR page:3) and are not carried here.

facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is defined in Q3 10-Q page:33 as net income from continuing operations plus taxes, other income and expense, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, impairments, legal reserves and settlements, restructuring, transaction expenses and non-recurring items. Reported-basis bridge for nine months 2026, recomputed from printed lines: operating income of -321.6 plus depreciation and amortization of 56.5 plus the goodwill impairment of 369.5 gives 104.4; adding stock-based compensation 50.5, restructuring 7.8, legal reserves and other 1.9, transaction expenses 4.1 and deducting the 4.8 fraud recovery gives 163.9, which equals the reported figure (Q3 PR page:12-13; Q3 10-Q page:34-37). The Q3 2026 bridge is 51.7 plus 15.3, 0.9, 2.6 and 0.6 giving 71.1. Largest definitional sensitivity: stock-based compensation is an add-back of 70.2 over the LTM, so EBITDA after stock-based compensation is 137.1 and gross leverage on that basis is 6.08x. The Term Loan B has no financial covenant; the revolver covenant definition of total net leverage is not supplied, so none of the ratios here is the covenant ratio.

facts.label: Revenue durability
facts.text: Evidence: management states that Hotels and Other "will continue to be impacted" by search placement changes (Q3 10-Q page:41) and two advertisers were about 21% of FY2025 revenue (10-K page:26). Mechanic: advertiser spending and organic traffic fall together when search results favour the search engine's own products. Implication: the segment that supplied about 69% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (financial handoff) has the weakest revenue visibility, which raises default risk if erosion continues faster than Experiences earnings grow.
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Margin and cash-flow risk
facts.text: Evidence: marketing is the largest cost; second-half experience cash flows are negative; pay-later usage may increase (Q3 10-Q page:64). Mechanic: operator payables fund cash during the first half and unwind in the second half. Implication: liquidity must be judged net of deferred merchant payables, and free cash flow can be negative over a year even with positive earnings.
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Tripadvisor, Inc. is in the middle of a deliberate change of business mix, and the creditor question is whether the new mix earns enough to carry the debt before the old mix erodes further. The old core, Hotels and Other, earns click-based and media advertising from travel partners and depends on traffic from search engines; management itself says search placement changes and AI overviews are reducing that traffic and that the segment will keep being affected. The new core, Experiences, is a commission-based marketplace for tours and activities led by Viator, which grew through 2025 but turned negative in the third quarter of 2026 after macro disruptions, higher cancellations and weaker Tripadvisor point-of-sale traffic. Against that, the company repaid its convertible notes in cash in April 2026, sold TheFork to American Express with closing on November 1, 2026 for about 741.0 of net cash, and started a further restructuring plan on November 4, 2026. Ownership changed in April 2025 when the merger with LTRIP removed the controlling stockholder, so there is no sponsor and no documented extraction by an owner, but also no anchor holder, and a cooperation agreement of March 22, 2026 and shareholder activism costs show outside pressure on strategy. What cannot be assessed from the pack is legal capacity: the credit agreement, the sale agreements and the beneficial ownership table are not supplied, so restrictions on asset sales, prepayment of sale proceeds and investor control are known only from filing summaries. The financial scale of these points is in the financial handoff: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 207.3, debt principal of 833.9 and cash of 706.8 before the sale proceeds.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one transaction in the period is the sale of TheFork, the company's European online restaurant reservation and management platform, to American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (a strategic buyer; no sponsor is involved). On June 14, 2026 the company entered into a put option agreement to sell the legal entities comprising TheFork "for $700.0 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments", and the Q3 10-Q states that American Express "provided an irrevocable commitment to acquire TheFork" (Q3 10-Q page:11). After the French Works Council consultation completed on July 30, 2026, the company exercised the put on August 1, 2026 and signed the Equity Purchase Agreement on August 2, 2026. The sale closed on November 1, 2026; the Q3 10-Q states "The total net cash consideration received at closing was approximately $741.0 million", reflecting adjustments for closing working capital, cash and indebtedness and net of transaction expenses; management expects a fourth-quarter 2026 gain of approximately $487.0 million and transaction costs of $16.0 million to $18.0 million netted against the gain, and warns that both amounts "may differ materially" (Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:65). Status: closed, with final adjustments still open. Accounting: TheFork was classified as held for sale and as a discontinued operation from the second quarter of 2026, with assets held for sale of 290.7 and liabilities held for sale of 62.3 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12 and page:16), and an accumulated other comprehensive loss of 21.4 to be netted against the gain (page:17). A Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months, for finance, information technology, human resources and other administrative services, started at closing (page:12-13), and the company expects no significant effect on future operating cash flows (page:65). Liquidity effect: the proceeds arrived after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are in no reported cash figure; management states that the proceeds provide "additional flexibility in its capital structure", that it "will continue to maintain optionality with respect to its use of the net proceeds", and that it "currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" (Q3 10-Q page:65). That is a Management Language statement of intent, not an executed commitment, and the pack does not show whether the Term Loan B can be prepaid with sale proceeds or whether the credit agreement requires any mandatory prepayment from asset sales, because the credit agreement is not supplied. Credit effect, analyst reading: the sale removes a segment that contributed 221 of FY2025 consolidated revenue (10-K page:189) and, with it, diversification away from advertising, but it leaves the capital structure unchanged until proceeds are applied, and it adds to cash against a term loan of 833.9.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues: none in 2026. The company raised no new debt in the first nine months of 2026; the only debt movement was the April 1, 2026 repayment of the 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes at maturity for $345.4 million including interest, funded by cash on hand, after which the capped calls expired unexercised (Q3 10-Q page:25-26). Earlier issues that define the present structure: the $500 million Term Loan B Facility issued July 8, 2024 at 99.75% of par, used to redeem the $500 million 2025 Senior Notes on July 15, 2024; the $350 million tack-on of March 20, 2025 at 98.56% of par, also due July 8, 2031 at SOFR plus 2.75%; and the Third Amendment of June 5, 2025, which redefined the revolver's springing maturity by reference to the 2026 notes and a cash test (10-K page:91 and page:160-163). Analyst reading: because the condition refers to notes outstanding of $200 million or more, it appears moot now that the notes are repaid, but the amended text itself is not in the pack. The revolver of $500.0 million matures June 29, 2028 and is undrawn.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Other transactions in the history that bear on the creditor: the merger with LTRIP, which closed on April 29, 2025 at an aggregate transaction price of $437 million, accounted for as a repurchase of the company's own shares held by LTRIP; before it, on March 20, 2025, the company lent LTRIP $326.7 million (about $327 million) so LTRIP could settle its exchangeable debentures, and that loan balance was folded into the transaction price (Q3 10-Q page:10; 10-K page:72). The aggregate cash paid including expenses was $410.7 million, plus 3,037,959 shares valued at about $38.9 million, less $13.1 million of LTRIP tax losses retained (Q3 10-Q page:10). The sources state that the tack-on proceeds were used to repay the 2026 notes; they do not state that the tack-on funded the merger. As an analyst reading only, gross debt rose by about 341 during 2025 while about 450.7 left the company in the merger repurchase and share buyback, and the notes were then repaid from cash in 2026; the filings do not link the two flows. A further restructuring plan was initiated on November 4, 2026 for the Hotels and Other segment with expected pre-tax costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million (Q3 10-Q page:37), and the Q3 release adds that management expects annualized gross savings of approximately $40 million (Q3 PR page:3), a release-only management claim that does not appear in the 10-Q.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Tripadvisor, Inc. is a moderately leveraged credit with ample near-term liquidity and no large maturity before 2031, but its earnings base is shrinking and the case rests on whether Experiences can replace Hotels and Other earnings. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million (cash of USD 706.8 million plus an undrawn USD 497.7 million revolver), a single term loan of USD 833.9 million with no financial covenant, and about USD 741.0 million of new sale proceeds. The weakest point is falling earnings: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million compares with USD 294.7 million in FY2025, and Hotels and Other supplies about 69% of it. What decides the outcome is how quickly that segment erodes and whether the sale proceeds reduce debt.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Tripadvisor's earnings fell sharply in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 71.1 million in Q3 2026 against USD 107.8 million a year earlier, and USD 163.9 million over nine months against USD 251.3 million, so LTM Adjusted EBITDA is USD 207.3 million against USD 294.7 million for FY2025 on revenue of USD 1,559.1 million over the LTM period [CP-1]. The decline is concentrated in Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and which took a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million. Hotels and Other still produced USD 143.6 million of the USD 207.3 million LTM Adjusted EBITDA, at a margin of 23.0%, while Experiences produced USD 63.7 million at a margin of 6.8% [CP-1]. The business therefore leans on the segment management expects to keep being hurt by search changes, which is the most important fact for the credit.

facts.text: Tripadvisor's debt is simple: one Term Loan B of USD 833.9 million due July 8, 2031, no financial covenant on that loan, and an undrawn USD 500.0 million revolver due June 29, 2028, after the USD 345.0 million convertible notes were repaid from cash on April 1, 2026 [CP-1]. Gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 because debt and earnings fell by similar proportions; net of cash it is 0.61x, but net of the operator payables that sit against the cash it is 2.53x, and after deducting stock-based compensation the gross ratio is 6.08x [CP-1]. LTM interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x, down from 4.99x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The revolver carries a maximum total net leverage covenant whose reported ratio is not printed, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1].

facts.text: Tripadvisor's liquidity is large but seasonal. Cash of USD 706.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 497.7 million give USD 1,204.5 million, or USD 807.7 million after deducting deferred merchant payables of USD 396.8 million owed to experience operators [CP-1]. Operating cash flow was negative USD 122.0 million in Q3 2026, LTM operating cash flow is USD 27.4 million, and LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million, because experience bookings bring cash in during the first half and reverse in the second half [CP-1, CP-1A]. Scheduled term loan amortisation is only USD 8.5 million a year, with USD 797.8 million due in 2031 [CP-1].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Tripadvisor has liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million against debt of USD 833.9 million and no financial covenant on the term loan, which removes near-term refinancing and covenant pressure; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Its capital structure is a single term loan due 2031 with amortisation of USD 8.5 million a year, after the convertible notes were repaid in cash, which keeps debt service predictable apart from the floating rate; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1, CP-1A]. The TheFork sale added about USD 741.0 million of net cash on November 1, 2026, which creates the option to cut debt; the closing is a Documentary Fact and the debt-reduction intent is Management Language, qualified as not a commitment [CP-1A]. Experiences volumes are still growing, with bookings up about 6% and gross booking value up about 5% over nine months 2026, which supports the replacement thesis even though Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026; this is a Documentary Fact with an Analyst Interpretation on what it means [CP-1A]. Capital spending of USD 31.8 million over nine months 2026 is light relative to revenue and can be flexed, so free cash flow is driven by operating cash flow; this is an Analyst Interpretation of Documentary Facts [CP-1, CP-1A]. There is no controlling stockholder or sponsor, no dividends, and no buybacks in 2026, which limits value leakage; this is an Analyst Interpretation of documented actions [CP-1A].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Tripadvisor's earnings are falling and concentrated: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million is down from USD 294.7 million for FY2025, with about 69% from Hotels and Other, a segment with a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million and a margin that Experiences, at 6.8%, does not yet replace; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. The segment that earns most depends on search traffic from a partner that also competes, and Booking and Expedia together were about 21% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so a ranking or advertiser change can cut earnings quickly; the facts are Documentary and the mechanism is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. Cash conversion is weak: LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million and reported cash is matched by USD 396.8 million of deferred merchant payables, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Leverage looks lower than it is because Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation: gross leverage is 4.02x on Adjusted EBITDA and 6.08x after stock-based compensation, and cash interest cover falls from 3.50x to 2.32x; this is an Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 figures [CP-1]. The term loan rate floats and the 10-K says it is not hedged, so a rate rise reduces cover while earnings fall; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Governance depends on a board facing activism with no anchor holder, so portfolio actions that affect lenders are plausible and the credit agreement protections are unknown; this is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. The synthesis cannot test creditor protections, covenant headroom or post-sale net debt from the supplied sources; this is Insufficient Information and is not treated as adverse.

spans.text: # CP-0 Source readiness for TripAdvisor, Inc. (trip), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Issuer: TripAdvisor, Inc. (ticker TRIP, run issuer id trip), the Nevada registrant that files the supplied reports under Commission file number 001-35362. As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD, which the filings use throughout. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026). Prior period: FY2025.

Question answered by this handoff: can the pinned source set support the downstream modules CP-1 (financial facts), CP-1A (business and transaction context), CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) and CP-5 (evidence trace and research QA), and what remains blocked. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates nothing. Context fields for borrower, parent, guarantors, ratings, quotes, deal terms and research questions are blank in the run context; blank is treated as not supplied, never as zero.
No upstream handoff exists for this module; it is the first in the sequence.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

### Files in the pack folder that are not pinned sources

### Supplied handoffs

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven pinned filings and releases can support a bounded credit snapshot of Tripadvisor, with limitations. The binding caveats are a changed reporting perimeter after the restaurant platform sale and the absence of the lender documents. | Medium | Annual and first-quarter filings include the sold restaurant business; annual continuing figures appear only in a management release; no credit agreement, covenant ratio or ratings are supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases are all present, and the latest release is dated on the cutoff day. | Debt, liquidity and cash flow can be sourced to filed statements rather than to management claims alone. | High |

| The annual report and first-quarter documents include the sold restaurant business, while later documents present it as discontinued. | Leverage and coverage must not mix perimeters, and the like-for-like annual base rests on a management release, not a filing. | Medium |

| Debt terms come only from filing notes. The credit agreement, covenant calculation and guarantor detail are not supplied. | Covenant headroom and collateral cannot be tested beyond management's statement of compliance. | Medium |

| The restaurant sale closed after quarter end and a new restructuring plan began the day before the cutoff. | Cash and debt after the quarter end are in no balance sheet, and use of sale proceeds is management intent only. | Medium |
| No credit ratings, bond quotes or forward guidance are supplied. | Relative value and rating-based views cannot be supported from this pack. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for source-level work on Tripadvisor, Inc. across all four requested modules, with bounded limitations, so each consumer is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and none is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. The evidence is strongest where it is a filed statement: the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q carries the latest balance sheet, debt note, liquidity discussion, goodwill impairment note and subsequent events, and the audited 10-K carries the debt, covenant and security terms. The strongest contrary evidence is a perimeter break. The 10-K, the Q1 10-Q and the Q1 release present TheFork inside the consolidated results, while the Q2 and Q3 10-Qs and releases present only continuing operations with prior periods recast. A downstream reader who joins the annual figures to the latest quarter without noticing this will overstate or understate trends. What cannot proceed from these sources is any test that needs the executed credit agreement, the covenant computation, ratings or market prices, a filed continuing-operations full-year base, or a post-closing balance sheet. The next evidence action is to obtain the Amended Credit Agreement and its three amendments, which the 10-K exhibit index lists as exhibits filed by reference, and to carry the perimeter label on every figure into CP-1. Source sufficiency is established here only; completion of the downstream analysis is not asserted.
### Source-by-source assessment

Each row records what the located text shows. A successful extraction is not a fidelity review: the extraction flattens tables into one cell per line, so column alignment must be checked against the cited page by the consumer. Images, charts and speaker notes were not inspected and no decks are in the pack.
| Source | What located text establishes (evidence) | Authority and extraction notes | Consequence for consumers |

| 10-K FY2025 | page:1 cover: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025", registrant TRIPADVISOR, INC., file number 001-35362. page:160-165 debt note; page:161 states the revolver covenant and security; page:192-193 exhibit index lists the credit agreement and three amendments. | Audited; whole USD millions, so figures are rounded to the nearest million and are not to be netted against one-decimal 10-Q figures without a rounding label. Includes TheFork in consolidated and segment data (page:185). | Source for the FY2025 base on the old perimeter and for the contractual debt terms. Not a continuing-operations base. |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | page:1 cover period March 31, 2026; page:43 debt and liquidity; page:36 TheFork segment discussion. | Unaudited; one decimal. Pre-recast perimeter, so its income statement and cash flows include TheFork. | Used only with a perimeter label; the first-quarter continuing-operations figures are not printed in it. |

| 10-Q Q2 2026 | page:1 cover period June 30, 2026; page:10-11 TheFork put option and held-for-sale; page:15-16 discontinued operations tables; page:55 debt and liquidity. | Unaudited; first filing on the recast perimeter. | Source for six-month and second-quarter continuing figures and for the first disclosure of the sale. |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | page:1 cover period September 30, 2026; page:3 balance sheet; page:6-7 cash flows; page:11-12 sale and discontinued presentation; page:22-23 goodwill; page:25-26 debt; page:37 subsequent events; page:61-66 liquidity. | Unaudited; the latest balance sheet and the comparative December 31, 2025 column recast for held-for-sale lines. | Primary source for the current position. Controls over the Q3 release where the two differ. |

| EX-99.1 Q1 release | page:1 summary table with TheFork as a segment. | Management narrative and non-GAAP reconciliations (page:11-15). Supports, never overrides, the 10-Q. | Attributed management claims and Adjusted EBITDA bridges on the pre-recast perimeter. |

| EX-99.1 Q2 release | page:1 pending sale; page:2 continuing operations highlights. | Supporting claims with reconciliations (page:12-16). | Bridge from the pre-recast to the recast perimeter in management's words. |

| EX-99.1 Q3 release | page:1 headline figures; page:3 restructuring action and goodwill impairment narrative; page:12-16 reconciliations and quarterly supplemental tables. | Supporting claims. Contains management claims not repeated in the 10-Q, for example expected annualized savings. | Attributed management claim only; a figure stated here alone cannot be carried as a filed fact. |
### Perimeter and period register
The perimeter changed during 2026 and the supplied sources straddle the change. Evidence for the break:
- Q2 release, page:1: "As a result of the pending transaction, the financial results of TheFork are classified as discontinued operations, and are no longer a reportable segment."
- Q3 10-Q, page:12: "the financial results of TheFork business are classified as discontinued operations in the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for all periods presented".

- The December 31, 2025 comparative in the Q3 10-Q is recast: goodwill is 724.2 there (page:3) against 844 in the 10-K balance sheet (page:108), and TheFork goodwill of 112.4 and 119.7 is shown separately as held for sale (page:16). The 10-K balance sheet and the Q3 10-Q comparative therefore describe different perimeters for the same date.

Mechanism and consequence: a trend or leverage metric that divides a figure from one perimeter by a figure from the other mixes the sold business into one side only. CP-1 must label every figure by perimeter and period, and CP-2 and CP-5 inherit that label. Cash is the clearest case: the Q3 10-Q balance sheet reports cash and cash equivalents of 706.8 for continuing operations, while the cash flow statement ends at 750.1 including restricted cash and discontinued operations, with 43.3 attributed to discontinued operations (page:6). These are different captions and perimeters, not a conflict.

Period labels the consumers will meet: three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025; three and six months ended June 30; three months ended March 31; FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 in the 10-K. No LTM or trailing figure is printed in any pinned source (searched the Q3 10-Q and Q3 release for twelve-month, trailing and LTM wording; only descriptive year references were found). The Q3 release does carry, at page:12-16, supplemental tables from continuing operations with each 2025 quarter, the 2025 full year and the 2026 quarters and year to date, covering revenue by segment, GAAP net income, Adjusted EBITDA, operating cash flow, capital expenditures and free cash flow. That gives a continuing-operations quarterly series at management-release authority only; the table footnote says full-year totals are as reported and may differ from the sum of the quarters because of rounding. The corresponding filed statements for the 2025 full year and fourth quarter on the continuing perimeter (operating income, interest expense, interest income, cash flow statement, cash paid for interest and taxes) are not in the pack.
### Entity and instrument roles located in the sources
- Issuer and registrant: Tripadvisor, Inc., a Nevada corporation (Q3 10-Q page:1). The 10-K records redomestication from Delaware to Nevada effective April 29, 2025 (10-K page:17).

- Borrowers under the credit agreement: the 10-K exhibit index names "Tripadvisor, Inc., Tripadvisor Holdings, LLC, Tripadvisor, LLC, the other Borrowers party thereto" with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent (10-K page:192). The context names no separate borrower or guarantor, so the borrower group and the "Subsidiary Loan Parties" that grant security (10-K page:161) are unresolved distinctions, carried as a gap.

- Instruments located: a revolving Credit Facility of 500.0 maturing June 29, 2028; a Term Loan B Facility of 500.0 issued July 8, 2024 plus a 350.0 tack-on of March 20, 2025, maturing July 8, 2031 at SOFR plus 2.75% (Q3 10-Q page:25); 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes, repaid at maturity on April 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:25-26). Q3 10-Q page:62 states "an aggregate principal amount remaining of $833.9 million" on the term loan and "The Term Loan B Facility has no financial covenants."

- Covenant evidence: 10-K page:161 states the Amended Credit Agreement "requires us to maintain a maximum total net leverage ratio of 4.5 to 1.0 solely in respect to the Credit Facility". The Q3 10-Q page:62 repeats only that a maximum total net leverage ratio applies and that "we were in compliance with our covenant requirements in effect under the Credit Facility"; it prints no level and no computed ratio.
- Security: 10-K page:161 states obligations are "secured by substantially all assets" of the company and the Subsidiary Loan Parties under the Security Documents.
- Unaudited versus audited: only the 10-K is audited; the three 10-Qs and three releases are unaudited, and the releases are management documents.
### Conflicts and unreconciled differences
| Item | Located statements | Downstream effect | Severity |

| Term loan rate at September 30, 2026 | Q3 10-Q page:25 gives an effective interest rate of 6.92%; Q3 10-Q page:62 gives "the interest rate on the Term Loan B Facility was 6.65%" at the same date. The second figure is not labelled effective or contractual. | Cost-of-debt and interest-coverage work must state which rate is used. Not reconciled here. | Low |

| Letters of credit at December 31, 2025 | 10-K page:161 gives $4 million; Q3 10-Q page:62 gives $3.6 million for the same date. | Rounding of whole millions versus one decimal; use the one-decimal figure for liquidity. | Low |

| Net loss for Q3 2026 | Q3 release page:1 headline net loss is on continuing operations (316.9); the Q3 10-Q consolidated statements show net loss including discontinued operations (313.1). | A perimeter difference stated in both documents, not an error; label which is used. | Low |

| Wording on the retired 2026 notes | 10-K page:164-165 calls the 2026 Senior Notes "senior unsecured obligations"; Q3 10-Q page:25 says "the related security interest and liens have been released" on repayment. | Possible springing or shared collateral wording that the pack cannot resolve; relevant only to history of the capital structure now that the notes are repaid. | Low |
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand and what the sources supply | Carried limitations |

| CP-1 financial facts | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs statements, quarter versus year-to-date, segments, add-backs, facility-level debt, cash-paid interest and taxes. Supplied: Q3 10-Q statements, segment note (page:33-37), debt note (page:25-26), cash paid for interest and taxes (page:6-7), non-GAAP reconciliations in the releases. | Perimeter break; LTM is not printed and the FY2025 continuing series exists only in the Q3 release supplemental tables (management authority); covenant ratio not printed; 10-K in whole millions; Q1 2026 continuing figures are in no filing and only in the Q3 release tables. |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs ownership, business model and change history. Supplied: business description (10-K page:4-6, Q3 10-Q page:39-41), the LTRIP merger (10-K page:17, 111-112), the TheFork sale (Q3 10-Q page:11-12, 42), restructuring (page:43-44), the goodwill impairment (page:22-23, 43). | The Equity Purchase Agreement and Transition Services Agreement are described, not supplied; sale proceeds and gain are stated as approximate and subject to adjustment; the savings claim is a management statement in the Q3 release. |

| CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Works from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs only; the source set does not prevent that. | Inherits every CP-1 and CP-1A limitation. Its dependency on those handoffs is sequenced by the planner and is not a source condition. |

| CP-5 evidence trace and QA | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs locators that can be reopened. All seven sources are retained in full, so citations resolve to `page:N`. | Table cells are flattened in extraction; derived figures require recomputation by CP-5 from cited components. |
None of the four consumers is marked DO NOT RUN.
### Management claims versus filed facts

The Q3 release (page:3) states that the November 4, 2026 restructuring "is expected to result in total company annualized gross savings of approximately $40 million". The Q3 10-Q (page:37, page:43) gives the plan date and a cost range but this savings figure was not found in the 10-Q. It is an attributed management claim and must stay labelled as such. Likewise the expected gain on the TheFork sale and the intended use of proceeds are management statements: the Q3 10-Q (page:65) says "management currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" and that it "will continue to maintain optionality", which is intent, not an executed commitment.
### Subsequent events and cutoff handling

Events after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date but on or before the 2026-11-05 cutoff, per the Q3 10-Q (page:11, page:37): the sale of TheFork closed on November 1, 2026 with approximately 741.0 of net cash consideration and an expected fourth-quarter gain of about 487.0, both "subject to change"; a Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months with American Express started at closing (page:12-13); a restructuring plan began on November 4, 2026 with expected pre-tax costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million (page:37). No pinned source is dated after the cutoff. The Q3 10-Q cover share count is as of October 30, 2026, before the cutoff.
## Calculations

None. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures above are reproduced exactly as printed, with their locator, and are not combined. The only counts are source page counts (194, 53, 65, 72, 20, 21 and 21 pages for the seven sources, all retained) taken from the extraction files.
## Gaps
Each gap names the missing input, the consumers it affects, why it matters and the remediation.
| Gap | Missing input and searches made | Affected consumers | Why it matters | Remediation |

| Lender documents | Not supplied: the Amended Credit Agreement, its First, Second and Third Amendments and the Security Documents. They are listed in the 10-K exhibit index (page:192-193) but their text is not in the pack. Searched all seven sources for the covenant definitions; only note summaries were found. | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5 | Covenant definition of total net leverage, add-backs, baskets, springing maturity terms and guarantor perimeter cannot be verified. | Obtain the exhibits from the filings that incorporate them. |

| Covenant computation | Not supplied: the issuer's computed total net leverage ratio. Level 4.5 to 1.0 appears only in the 10-K (page:161); the 2026 10-Qs state compliance without a ratio. | CP-1, CP-2 | Headroom cannot be sourced; any derived ratio would use a different definition. | Treat as Not calculable until the compliance certificate or definition is obtained. |

| Filed continuing-operations annual base | Not supplied as a filing: FY2025 and Q4 2025 operating income, interest expense, interest income, cash flow statement and cash paid for interest and taxes on the continuing perimeter, and any printed LTM figure. Supplied only at management-release authority: quarterly 2025 and 2026 revenue, GAAP net income, Adjusted EBITDA, operating cash flow, capital expenditures and free cash flow (Q3 release page:12-16). Nine-month 2025 comparatives in the Q3 10-Q are recast. | CP-1, CP-2 | Leverage and coverage on the post-sale perimeter rest on non-GAAP and unaudited management tables for the Q4 2025 leg; interest coverage on a continuing basis cannot be completed for that leg. | CP-1 may build LTM Adjusted EBITDA and LTM operating cash flow from the release quarters with a calculation shown and the authority labelled; interest for the Q4 2025 leg is Not supplied. |

| Q1 2026 continuing-operations discrete figures | Not printed in the Q1 filing or Q1 release, which include TheFork; the Q3 release supplemental tables (page:12-16) print a first-quarter 2026 continuing column, and the Q2 10-Q gives the six-month continuing result. | CP-1 | The first-quarter continuing figures are available only at management-release authority. | CP-1 to cite the release column and cross-check it against the Q2 and Q3 10-Q year-to-date figures. |

| TheFork sale documents | Not supplied: the Equity Purchase Agreement of August 2, 2026, the Put Option Agreement of June 14, 2026 and the Transition Services Agreement. Terms are known only from the 10-Q and releases. | CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5 | Final consideration, adjustments, indemnities and the proceeds waterfall cannot be confirmed. | Treat the sale terms as filed disclosure, not executed-document evidence. |

| Post-closing capital structure | Not supplied: any balance sheet or debt balance after November 1, 2026, or any commitment to repay the term loan. | CP-1, CP-2 | The roughly 741.0 of proceeds is not in any statement; intended debt reduction is not an executed action. | Revisit when the next periodic report is filed (not available by the cutoff). |

| Ratings, market data and guidance | Not supplied: credit ratings, bond or loan quotes, valuation inputs or forward guidance (searched sources for rating agency names and outlook wording; none found; the context ratings and quotes fields are empty). The only market reference is the statement in the goodwill note that the stock price fell nearly 40% from June 30 to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:22). | CP-2 | No rating or market-implied cross-check is possible. | External sources would be needed and would have to be labelled external. |

| Presentations and charts | No investor presentation or decks are in the pack; earnings releases stand in. Text extraction only; no chart or image content was inspected. | CP-1, CP-1A | Visual or slide-only disclosures, if any exist, are not covered. | None for this run. |

| Guarantors and restricted group | The Subsidiary Loan Parties and guarantors under the credit agreement are not named in the pack; the context lists none. | CP-1A, CP-2 | Structural subordination and collateral reach cannot be assessed beyond the "substantially all assets" statement. | Obtain the guarantee and security schedules. |

| Extraction fidelity | Flattened table cells; the first page of each file carries the original HTML hash rather than the pinned hash. No fidelity review was performed. | All | Column misalignment risk when reading numeric tables. | Consumers reopen each cited page and confirm labels, signs and periods. |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1 on all seven sources. Instructions carried forward: label every figure with its period and perimeter (consolidated including TheFork, or continuing operations with TheFork discontinued); keep the 10-K in whole millions and the 10-Qs in one decimal; take the current position from the Q3 2026 10-Q and use the releases only as attributed management support; reproduce the covenant statement as qualitative compliance without inventing a ratio; build any LTM figure only from the Q3 release quarterly continuing tables (page:12-16) with the calculation shown and the management authority labelled, and mark the filed FY2025 continuing statements, Q4 2025 interest and post-closing figures as Not supplied or Not calculable; and cite the Q3 10-Q page numbers given above for the debt, liquidity, goodwill and subsequent-event items. CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 follow in dependency order and inherit this handoff's limitations.

| Hotels and Other produced 143.6 of the 207.3 LTM Adjusted EBITDA while its revenue fell, and it took a 369.5 goodwill impairment in Q3 2026. | Debt service leans on a shrinking segment while the growth segment earns little, so earnings quality is the central credit question. | Medium |

| Debt is one Term Loan B of 833.9 due 2031 plus an undrawn 500.0 revolver due 2028; the 345.0 convertible notes were repaid on April 1, 2026. | No maturity of size before 2031 and no financial covenant on the term loan, but the rate floats and the 10-K says it is unhedged. | High |

| Operating cash flow was -122.0 in Q3 2026 and LTM free cash flow is -17.5; cash of 706.8 sits beside 396.8 of deferred merchant payables. | Reported cash overstates freely usable cash, and seasonal outflows can absorb much of it in the second half. | Medium |

| The sale of TheFork closed after quarter end for about 741.0 of net cash, which no reported balance sheet includes. | Net debt could fall sharply, but only management intent, not a commitment, links the proceeds to debt reduction. | Medium |
### Financial base view

TripAdvisor, Inc. enters the fourth quarter of 2026 with a lower-earning but lower-debt capital structure than a year ago. On the continuing-operations perimeter, LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 207.3 against 294.7 for FY2025, driven by Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026, while Experiences revenue fell 3% in the same quarter after growing earlier in the year. Debt principal has fallen from 1,185 at December 31, 2025 to 833.9 at September 30, 2026 because the 345.0 convertible notes were repaid in cash on April 1, 2026, so gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 only because EBITDA and debt fell together. Net of 706.8 of cash the ratio is 0.61x, but 396.8 of deferred merchant payables, amounts owed to experience operators after travel, sit against that cash, and on a cash-less-float basis net leverage is 2.53x. Free cash flow is negative on an LTM basis, interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x LTM, and the term loan has no financial covenant while the revolver carries a leverage maximum whose reported level is not printed in the 2026 filings. The TheFork sale added about 741.0 of net cash on November 1, 2026, after the balance sheet date, so the reported figures understate the post-sale cash position. Every ratio below rests on management Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, so the ratios are better read as a ceiling on earnings capacity than as a covenant calculation.

### Segment and earnings quality drivers

Hotels and Other revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and 21% over nine months, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 41% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 (Q3 PR page:1 and page:14). Management attributes the decline to "the sustained acceleration of traffic acquisition headwinds negatively impacting this business due to the changes in the search landscape" (Q3 10-Q page:22), which reads as a structural rather than cyclical explanation (analyst reading). Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026 after growing 1% over nine months, with Adjusted EBITDA down 27% in Q3 2026; the 10-Q cites macro events, cancellations and search headwinds on the Tripadvisor point of sale (Q3 10-Q page:43 and page:49). Mechanism: the segment that supplies about 69% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is the one in structural decline, and the growth segment's LTM margin is 6.8% against 23.0% for Hotels and Other, so group margin falls as mix shifts even before any further decline in Hotels and Other. Credit implication: debt capacity depends on how fast Hotels and Other earnings erode against how fast Experiences margin can expand; the November 4, 2026 restructuring plan (costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million, Q3 10-Q page:37) targets the cost base but management's claimed savings are a release-only statement (Q3 PR page:3) and are not carried here.
### Definition review

Adjusted EBITDA is defined in Q3 10-Q page:33 as net income from continuing operations plus taxes, other income and expense, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, impairments, legal reserves and settlements, restructuring, transaction expenses and non-recurring items. Reported-basis bridge for nine months 2026, recomputed from printed lines: operating income of -321.6 plus depreciation and amortization of 56.5 plus the goodwill impairment of 369.5 gives 104.4; adding stock-based compensation 50.5, restructuring 7.8, legal reserves and other 1.9, transaction expenses 4.1 and deducting the 4.8 fraud recovery gives 163.9, which equals the reported figure (Q3 PR page:12-13; Q3 10-Q page:34-37). The Q3 2026 bridge is 51.7 plus 15.3, 0.9, 2.6 and 0.6 giving 71.1. Largest definitional sensitivity: stock-based compensation is an add-back of 70.2 over the LTM, so EBITDA after stock-based compensation is 137.1 and gross leverage on that basis is 6.08x. The Term Loan B has no financial covenant; the revolver covenant definition of total net leverage is not supplied, so none of the ratios here is the covenant ratio.

### Subsequent events

Per Q3 10-Q page:11, page:37 and Q3 PR page:2-3: the TheFork sale closed on November 1, 2026 with total net cash consideration of approximately 741.0 and an expected fourth-quarter gain of about 487.0, both subject to final adjustments; a Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months began at closing; and a restructuring plan was started on November 4, 2026 with expected pre-tax costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million. Management "currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" (Q3 10-Q page:65). None of these is in the September 30, 2026 balance sheet.
## Calculations
All inputs are printed in the cited locators. Amounts in USD millions. Results are rounded to the precision shown; ratios to two decimals.
### LTM Adjusted EBITDA, continuing operations

### Cash flow build

LTM operating cash flow: Q4 2025 -103.0 + 9M 2026 130.4 = 27.4. LTM capital expenditures: 13.1 + 31.8 = 44.9. LTM free cash flow: -116.1 + 98.6 = -17.5, equal to 27.4 - 44.9 = -17.5. FY2025 check: 234.7 - 61.3 = 173.4. 9M 2025 free cash flow: 337.5 - 48.2 = 289.3. LTM revenue: 355.0 + 1,204.1 = 1,559.1. LTM margin: 207.3 / 1,559.1 = 13.3%. LTM net income: -29.9 + -324.7 = -354.6. LTM depreciation and amortization: 19.2 + 56.5 = 75.7. LTM stock-based compensation: 19.7 + 50.5 = 70.2. LTM cash taxes: 29 - 20.3 + 8.7 = 17.4.
### Segment mix

LTM Hotels and Other Adjusted EBITDA: 29.1 + 114.5 = 143.6 of 207.3, which is 69.3%; Experiences 14.3 + 49.4 = 63.7, which is 30.7%. LTM segment margins: 143.6 / 624.1 = 23.0% (revenue 151.3 + 472.8 = 624.1); 63.7 / 935.0 = 6.8% (revenue 203.7 + 731.3 = 935.0). Year-on-year: Q3 2026 revenue 436.4 / 490.8 - 1 = -11.1%; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA 71.1 / 107.8 - 1 = -34.0%; nine-month revenue 1,204.1 / 1,319.3 - 1 = -8.7%; nine-month Adjusted EBITDA 163.9 / 251.3 - 1 = -34.8%.
### Liquidity and debt schedule

Liquidity at September 30, 2026: cash 706.8 + undrawn revolver 497.7 (500.0 - 2.3) = 1,204.5; less deferred merchant payables 396.8 = 807.7. At December 31, 2025: 978.0 + 496.4 = 1,474.4; less 308.1 = 1,166.3. Term Loan B at fair value: 795.8 / 833.9 = 95.4% of principal at September 30, 2026; 811.1 / 840.2 = 96.5% at December 31, 2025 (comparative as restated in the 10-Q). Maturity derivation: 833.9 principal; Q4 2026 installment 2.1; 2027 to 2030 installments 4 x 8.5 = 34.0; 2031 installments 4.2 before the July 8 balance; balance 833.9 - 2.1 - 34.0 - 4.2 = 793.6; 2031 total 4.2 + 793.6 = 797.8. Check: 2.1 + 34.0 + 797.8 = 833.9.
### Illustrative post-sale view (not a reported figure)

Principal 833.9 against cash of 706.8 plus net sale consideration of about 741.0 = 1,447.8 gives net cash of 613.9 (net debt -613.9; -613.9 / 207.3 = -2.96x). Net of operator float: 706.8 - 396.8 + 741.0 = 1,051.0; net debt -217.1. This ignores fourth-quarter seasonal operating cash outflow (Q4 2025 was -103.0), the $15 million to $20 million restructuring cost, any prepayment of debt and final purchase price adjustments, and is shown only to size the effect.

## Request

Issuer: TripAdvisor, Inc. (ticker TRIP), the Nevada registrant and sole reporting entity in the supplied filings. As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD. Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, and what is the credit-relevant change in the business? Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

Method points applied: every material conclusion runs from a located quote to a risk mechanic to a credit implication; every fact row carries one of the four tags Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information; conflicts are quoted and logged, never reconciled; governance is assessed at issuer level on documented actions only, with legal capacity, willingness and feasibility kept apart. ### Business and transaction view

Tripadvisor, Inc. is in the middle of a deliberate change of business mix, and the creditor question is whether the new mix earns enough to carry the debt before the old mix erodes further. The old core, Hotels and Other, earns click-based and media advertising from travel partners and depends on traffic from search engines; management itself says search placement changes and AI overviews are reducing that traffic and that the segment will keep being affected. The new core, Experiences, is a commission-based marketplace for tours and activities led by Viator, which grew through 2025 but turned negative in the third quarter of 2026 after macro disruptions, higher cancellations and weaker Tripadvisor point-of-sale traffic. Against that, the company repaid its convertible notes in cash in April 2026, sold TheFork to American Express with closing on November 1, 2026 for about 741.0 of net cash, and started a further restructuring plan on November 4, 2026. Ownership changed in April 2025 when the merger with LTRIP removed the controlling stockholder, so there is no sponsor and no documented extraction by an owner, but also no anchor holder, and a cooperation agreement of March 22, 2026 and shareholder activism costs show outside pressure on strategy. What cannot be assessed from the pack is legal capacity: the credit agreement, the sale agreements and the beneficial ownership table are not supplied, so restrictions on asset sales, prepayment of sale proceeds and investor control are known only from filing summaries. The financial scale of these points is in the financial handoff: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 207.3, debt principal of 833.9 and cash of 706.8 before the sale proceeds.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one transaction in the period is the sale of TheFork, the company's European online restaurant reservation and management platform, to American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (a strategic buyer; no sponsor is involved). On June 14, 2026 the company entered into a put option agreement to sell the legal entities comprising TheFork "for $700.0 million in cash, subject to certain adjustments", and the Q3 10-Q states that American Express "provided an irrevocable commitment to acquire TheFork" (Q3 10-Q page:11). After the French Works Council consultation completed on July 30, 2026, the company exercised the put on August 1, 2026 and signed the Equity Purchase Agreement on August 2, 2026. The sale closed on November 1, 2026; the Q3 10-Q states "The total net cash consideration received at closing was approximately $741.0 million", reflecting adjustments for closing working capital, cash and indebtedness and net of transaction expenses; management expects a fourth-quarter 2026 gain of approximately $487.0 million and transaction costs of $16.0 million to $18.0 million netted against the gain, and warns that both amounts "may differ materially" (Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:65). Status: closed, with final adjustments still open. Accounting: TheFork was classified as held for sale and as a discontinued operation from the second quarter of 2026, with assets held for sale of 290.7 and liabilities held for sale of 62.3 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12 and page:16), and an accumulated other comprehensive loss of 21.4 to be netted against the gain (page:17). A Transition Services Agreement of up to 12 months, for finance, information technology, human resources and other administrative services, started at closing (page:12-13), and the company expects no significant effect on future operating cash flows (page:65). Liquidity effect: the proceeds arrived after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are in no reported cash figure; management states that the proceeds provide "additional flexibility in its capital structure", that it "will continue to maintain optionality with respect to its use of the net proceeds", and that it "currently expects that the Company will prioritize reduction of its long-term debt" (Q3 10-Q page:65). That is a Management Language statement of intent, not an executed commitment, and the pack does not show whether the Term Loan B can be prepaid with sale proceeds or whether the credit agreement requires any mandatory prepayment from asset sales, because the credit agreement is not supplied. Credit effect, analyst reading: the sale removes a segment that contributed 221 of FY2025 consolidated revenue (10-K page:189) and, with it, diversification away from advertising, but it leaves the capital structure unchanged until proceeds are applied, and it adds to cash against a term loan of 833.9.

New debt issues: none in 2026. The company raised no new debt in the first nine months of 2026; the only debt movement was the April 1, 2026 repayment of the 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes at maturity for $345.4 million including interest, funded by cash on hand, after which the capped calls expired unexercised (Q3 10-Q page:25-26). Earlier issues that define the present structure: the $500 million Term Loan B Facility issued July 8, 2024 at 99.75% of par, used to redeem the $500 million 2025 Senior Notes on July 15, 2024; the $350 million tack-on of March 20, 2025 at 98.56% of par, also due July 8, 2031 at SOFR plus 2.75%; and the Third Amendment of June 5, 2025, which redefined the revolver's springing maturity by reference to the 2026 notes and a cash test (10-K page:91 and page:160-163). Analyst reading: because the condition refers to notes outstanding of $200 million or more, it appears moot now that the notes are repaid, but the amended text itself is not in the pack. The revolver of $500.0 million matures June 29, 2028 and is undrawn.

Other transactions in the history that bear on the creditor: the merger with LTRIP, which closed on April 29, 2025 at an aggregate transaction price of $437 million, accounted for as a repurchase of the company's own shares held by LTRIP; before it, on March 20, 2025, the company lent LTRIP $326.7 million (about $327 million) so LTRIP could settle its exchangeable debentures, and that loan balance was folded into the transaction price (Q3 10-Q page:10; 10-K page:72). The aggregate cash paid including expenses was $410.7 million, plus 3,037,959 shares valued at about $38.9 million, less $13.1 million of LTRIP tax losses retained (Q3 10-Q page:10). The sources state that the tack-on proceeds were used to repay the 2026 notes; they do not state that the tack-on funded the merger. As an analyst reading only, gross debt rose by about 341 during 2025 while about 450.7 left the company in the merger repurchase and share buyback, and the notes were then repaid from cash in 2026; the filings do not link the two flows. A further restructuring plan was initiated on November 4, 2026 for the Hotels and Other segment with expected pre-tax costs of approximately $15 million to $20 million (Q3 10-Q page:37), and the Q3 release adds that management expects annualized gross savings of approximately $40 million (Q3 PR page:3), a release-only management claim that does not appear in the 10-Q.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Tripadvisor has strong liquidity and no large maturity before 2031, but its earnings base is shrinking. Gross leverage is 4.02x, and the credit depends on Experiences replacing Hotels and Other earnings. | Medium | Ratios rest on management Adjusted EBITDA, and the credit agreement, covenant ratio and sale agreements are not supplied, so creditor protections are untested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| LTM Adjusted EBITDA is USD 207.3 million against USD 294.7 million for FY2025, and Hotels and Other supplies about 69% of it. | Debt service depends on the shrinking segment, so further decline raises leverage directly. | High |

| Liquidity is USD 1,204.5 million, and the only debt is a USD 833.9 million term loan due 2031 with no financial covenant. | No refinancing or covenant pressure is visible near term, which gives time for the strategy to work. | High |

| Operating cash flow was negative USD 122.0 million in Q3 2026 and LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million. | Seasonal outflows and operator payables absorb much of the cash balance, so usable liquidity is lower than reported. | Medium |

| The TheFork sale closed on November 1, 2026 for about USD 741.0 million of net cash, and management expects to prioritise debt reduction. | Leverage could fall quickly if proceeds repay debt, but intent is not a commitment and prepayment terms are unknown. | Medium |

| No controlling stockholder or sponsor exists, activism costs and a cooperation agreement appeared in 2026, and no creditor-adverse action is documented. | Further portfolio actions are plausible, and lender protection depends on credit agreement terms that are not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

Tripadvisor, Inc. is a moderately leveraged credit with ample near-term liquidity and no large maturity before 2031, but its earnings base is shrinking and the case rests on whether Experiences can replace Hotels and Other earnings. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million (cash of USD 706.8 million plus an undrawn USD 497.7 million revolver), a single term loan of USD 833.9 million with no financial covenant, and about USD 741.0 million of new sale proceeds. The weakest point is falling earnings: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million compares with USD 294.7 million in FY2025, and Hotels and Other supplies about 69% of it. What decides the outcome is how quickly that segment erodes and whether the sale proceeds reduce debt.
### Key findings

Tripadvisor's earnings fell sharply in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 71.1 million in Q3 2026 against USD 107.8 million a year earlier, and USD 163.9 million over nine months against USD 251.3 million, so LTM Adjusted EBITDA is USD 207.3 million against USD 294.7 million for FY2025 on revenue of USD 1,559.1 million over the LTM period [CP-1]. The decline is concentrated in Hotels and Other, whose revenue fell 23% in Q3 2026 and which took a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million. Hotels and Other still produced USD 143.6 million of the USD 207.3 million LTM Adjusted EBITDA, at a margin of 23.0%, while Experiences produced USD 63.7 million at a margin of 6.8% [CP-1]. The business therefore leans on the segment management expects to keep being hurt by search changes, which is the most important fact for the credit.

Tripadvisor's debt is simple: one Term Loan B of USD 833.9 million due July 8, 2031, no financial covenant on that loan, and an undrawn USD 500.0 million revolver due June 29, 2028, after the USD 345.0 million convertible notes were repaid from cash on April 1, 2026 [CP-1]. Gross debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 4.02x, the same as at year end 2025 because debt and earnings fell by similar proportions; net of cash it is 0.61x, but net of the operator payables that sit against the cash it is 2.53x, and after deducting stock-based compensation the gross ratio is 6.08x [CP-1]. LTM interest cover on cash interest is 3.50x, down from 4.99x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The revolver carries a maximum total net leverage covenant whose reported ratio is not printed, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1].

Tripadvisor's liquidity is large but seasonal. Cash of USD 706.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 497.7 million give USD 1,204.5 million, or USD 807.7 million after deducting deferred merchant payables of USD 396.8 million owed to experience operators [CP-1]. Operating cash flow was negative USD 122.0 million in Q3 2026, LTM operating cash flow is USD 27.4 million, and LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million, because experience bookings bring cash in during the first half and reverse in the second half [CP-1, CP-1A]. Scheduled term loan amortisation is only USD 8.5 million a year, with USD 797.8 million due in 2031 [CP-1].

Tripadvisor completed the sale of TheFork to American Express on November 1, 2026 for about USD 741.0 million of net cash against a USD 700.0 million headline price, with an expected fourth-quarter gain of about USD 487.0 million. Management says it currently expects to prioritise reduction of long-term debt, but that is a stated intent, not an executed commitment, and whether the term loan can be prepaid from proceeds depends on a credit agreement that is not supplied [CP-1A]. On an illustrative basis, before seasonal outflow and restructuring cost, cash plus the proceeds would exceed the term loan by USD 613.9 million, which shows the size of the effect rather than a forecast [CP-1].

Tripadvisor has no controlling stockholder since the April 2025 merger with LTRIP and no sponsor, paid no dividends, bought back no shares in 2026 and repaid the notes from cash, which supports a creditor-friendly reading of behaviour; a cooperation agreement dated March 22, 2026 and USD 3.3 million of activism costs show outside pressure on strategy, and a restructuring plan for Hotels and Other began on November 4, 2026 [CP-1A]. No priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but the pack cannot show them either way because the credit agreement is missing [CP-1A].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Tripadvisor has liquidity of USD 1,204.5 million against debt of USD 833.9 million and no financial covenant on the term loan, which removes near-term refinancing and covenant pressure; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Its capital structure is a single term loan due 2031 with amortisation of USD 8.5 million a year, after the convertible notes were repaid in cash, which keeps debt service predictable apart from the floating rate; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1, CP-1A]. The TheFork sale added about USD 741.0 million of net cash on November 1, 2026, which creates the option to cut debt; the closing is a Documentary Fact and the debt-reduction intent is Management Language, qualified as not a commitment [CP-1A]. Experiences volumes are still growing, with bookings up about 6% and gross booking value up about 5% over nine months 2026, which supports the replacement thesis even though Experiences revenue fell 3% in Q3 2026; this is a Documentary Fact with an Analyst Interpretation on what it means [CP-1A]. Capital spending of USD 31.8 million over nine months 2026 is light relative to revenue and can be flexed, so free cash flow is driven by operating cash flow; this is an Analyst Interpretation of Documentary Facts [CP-1, CP-1A]. There is no controlling stockholder or sponsor, no dividends, and no buybacks in 2026, which limits value leakage; this is an Analyst Interpretation of documented actions [CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Tripadvisor's earnings are falling and concentrated: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 207.3 million is down from USD 294.7 million for FY2025, with about 69% from Hotels and Other, a segment with a goodwill impairment of USD 369.5 million and a margin that Experiences, at 6.8%, does not yet replace; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. The segment that earns most depends on search traffic from a partner that also competes, and Booking and Expedia together were about 21% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so a ranking or advertiser change can cut earnings quickly; the facts are Documentary and the mechanism is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. Cash conversion is weak: LTM free cash flow is negative USD 17.5 million and reported cash is matched by USD 396.8 million of deferred merchant payables, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Leverage looks lower than it is because Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation: gross leverage is 4.02x on Adjusted EBITDA and 6.08x after stock-based compensation, and cash interest cover falls from 3.50x to 2.32x; this is an Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 figures [CP-1]. The term loan rate floats and the 10-K says it is not hedged, so a rate rise reduces cover while earnings fall; this is a Documentary Fact [CP-1]. Governance depends on a board facing activism with no anchor holder, so portfolio actions that affect lenders are plausible and the credit agreement protections are unknown; this is an Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]. The synthesis cannot test creditor protections, covenant headroom or post-sale net debt from the supplied sources; this is Insufficient Information and is not treated as adverse.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Moderately leveraged on a gross basis (4.02x), low on a net basis (0.61x), with ample liquidity and no large maturity before 2031, offset by a shrinking earnings base that depends on one declining segment. The view is comfortable on near-term liquidity and cautious on the direction of earnings; it is not a rating or a recommendation. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and cash-flow figures; CP-1A business and transaction rows |

| Thesis | Tripadvisor can service and refinance its single term loan if Hotels and Other earnings erode slowly and the sale proceeds or Experiences growth restore earnings, but it has little room if search-driven declines accelerate before proceeds reduce debt. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category | Basis |

| Structural erosion of Hotels and Other | Search engines favour their own products and AI answers, cutting free traffic; the segment is click-advertising and depends on two travel partners. | Adjusted EBITDA falls faster than Experiences grows, raising leverage and cutting interest cover from 3.50x. | Material | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A business model and traffic rows; CP-1 segment figures |

| Seasonal and float-driven liquidity | Cash from bookings is held against deferred merchant payables and reverses in the second half, with pay-later usage able to increase. | Free cash flow can stay negative and reported cash overstates usable liquidity at the seasonal low. | Material | Documentary Fact | CP-1 cash flow and liquidity figures; CP-1A working-capital row |

| Leverage on a flattering EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation and other items; the covenant definition is unknown. | Reported ratios understate leverage, and covenant headroom cannot be measured. | Material | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 definition review and leverage figures |

| Use of sale proceeds and portfolio actions | Management states an intent to prioritise debt reduction while also pursuing value recognition across assets; asset-sale and prepayment terms are unknown. | Proceeds may reduce debt or fund other uses; further disposals could remove earnings that service the loan. | Material | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A transaction and governance rows |

| Disclosure gap on creditor protections | The credit agreement, collateral scope, guarantors and covenant certificate are not supplied. | Legal capacity, priming risk and recovery mechanics cannot be assessed; they are neither favourable nor adverse. | Material | Insufficient Information | CP-0 gaps; CP-1A gaps |

| Tax and legal contingencies | A possible additional UK tax liability and other tax audits are described, with a range for one item. | A cash outflow outside debt could reduce liquidity, though small against current cash. | Minor | Documentary Fact | CP-1 claims-outside-debt table |
## Calculations

None. This module is a synthesis; every figure above is carried unchanged from CP-1 and CP-1A, where the inputs and formulas are shown. The illustrative post-sale cash figure is CP-1's own calculation and is labelled illustrative there and here.
